item.title: Father questions delayed CT scan as Health Minister points to hospital space constraints

item.content:encoded:
The father of a 17-year-old boy is still waiting for his son to receive further medical assessment after he was unable to be transferred from Nadi Hospital to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan, with Health Minister Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu saying the issue is not a shortage of beds, but a shortage of hospital space.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Mohammed Kalam says his son was admitted to Nadi Hospital at around 5pm last Friday after he began bleeding from the nose and feeling weak.

Kalam says doctors planned to transfer his son to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan, but the family was later informed that there was no available bed.

He says they were told the transfer would take place on Sunday, but no bed became available, and the family eventually took their son home.

Kalam says they have still not received an update on when his son will be able to receive the required medical assessment.

He is questioning why there are not enough hospital beds to accommodate patients requiring specialised care.

Responding to questions from fijivillage News, Dr Lalabalavu says Fiji has hospital beds available, but the lack of physical space limits how many beds can be accommodated.

He says hospitals can only fit a certain number of beds within their allocated space.

Dr Lalabalavu says the Ministry of Health is working on a replacement and improvement programme.

He says Nadi Hospital now has a new ultrasound scan machine, while an existing X-ray table-mounted machine is also available.

However, Kalam's concern remains focused not only on his son's delayed access to further medical assessment and the CT scan, but also on other patients who may face similar challenges.

fijivillage News is continuing to follow up on the case and the availability of hospital beds and specialised services for patients requiring further assessment.

item.title: Students still waiting for subsidised bus cards as Term 3 approaches
item.description: Students who have been waiting for government-funded bus cards for months could face further uncertainty as Term 3 approaches, with concerns raised in Parliament over delays in the National Transport Assistance Scheme. The issue was raised in Parliament today following a question to the Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro, about how the Ministry plans to ensure government funded student cards a
item.content:encoded:
Students who have been waiting for government-funded bus cards for months could face further uncertainty as Term 3 approaches, with concerns raised in Parliament over delays in the National Transport Assistance Scheme.

The issue was raised in Parliament today following a question to the Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro, about how the Ministry plans to ensure government funded student cards are topped up on time in the future.

Radrodro says that eligible students must apply for transport assistance through their schools before the beginning of each school year.

He says applications are then assessed and verified by school heads before being processed by the Ministry.

Radrodro says for existing students, blue bus cards are expected to be topped up automatically during Terms 2 and 3.

The Ministry says cards are topped up twice each term, covering Weeks 1 to 7 and Weeks 8 to 14.

The Minister says delays could result from incomplete applications or information not being submitted and verified within the required timeframe.

He asked Opposition MP Hem Chand to provide the Ministry with a list of affected students and their details so the cases could be investigated and processed.

The Minister also reminded students to keep their cards safe.

Students who lose or damage their cards must apply for a replacement through their school and have the replacement activated through the Ministry's FEMIS system.

Radrodro says the Government has allocated $54 million in the 2026–27 Budget for student transport assistance. The programme supports more than 70,000 students through blue bus cards and more than 44,000 st udents through Rural Service Licences.

With Term 3 approaching, the immediate concern remains whether students who have already applied but are still waiting for their cards will receive them in time to avoid fu rther transport costs for their families.
